title: Fetch three CSVs over the web, merge, dedupe, report

turns.prompt: Three regional order exports are online: {FIXTURES}/orders-north.csv, {FIXTURES}/orders-south.csv and {FIXTURES}/orders-west.csv (columns order_id, date, region, product, amount). Some orders appear in more than one file. Download all three, merge them, remove duplicate orders (same order_id), and write {D}/orders-report.md with: the number of unique orders, how many duplicates you removed, the total amount, and the amount per region (two decimals). Save the merged, deduplicated data as {D}/orders-merged.csv. Then tell me the unique count and the total.
turns.verify: f={D}/orders-report.md; test -f $f || { echo FAIL: no report; exit 0; }; m={D}/orders-merged.csv; rows=$(test -f $m && tail -n +2 $m | grep -c . || echo 0); sed 's/^/SHOW /' $f | head -30; echo "SHOW merged_rows=$rows"; echo PASS

rubric.criteria: Report states unique orders, duplicates removed, total and per-region amounts with two decimals, clearly laid out; the merged CSV exists.
